title: Copilot Studio: share autonomous agents with end users (run-only)
summary: The roadmap dates, recipient licensing and environment-based billing are supported. Hold the briefing because it treats the embedded-maker-credentials control's applicability as unknown even though Microsoft explicitly exempts end-user-authenticated connections, which this sharing feature requires. The data-policy navigation also needs a small correction.

claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.claim: General Availability is targeted for January CY2027.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.claim: The roadmap describes autonomous agents as previously usable and manageable only by makers.
claims.quote: Previously, autonomous agents could only be used and managed by makers, limiting their reach to the people who needed them.

claims.claim: Run-only sharing extends autonomous agents to end users without edit permissions or ownership.
claims.quote: Run-only sharing enables makers to securely share autonomous agents with end users, allowing users to benefit from agent-driven automation without requiring edit permissions or ownership.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Makers can share a published agent with triggers for recipients to run using their own credentials.
claims.quote: You can share a published agent that has triggers with users who need to run the agent by using their own credentials. Before sharing, configure the agent's triggers and tools for user authentication.

claims.claim: The maker can select individual users or security groups as run-only recipients.
claims.quote: Enter the user name, email addresses of individual users, or security groups you want to share the agent with. Ensure Can use appears beside the search bar.

claims.claim: Learn documents this behaviour as preview or prerelease while the roadmap remains In development.
claims.quote:
Set up a shared autonomous agent (Microsoft Copilot) (preview)
[This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.where: controls[6].ui; Governance controls table; What's changing
claims.claim: The maker path for run-only access is Copilot Studio > Agents > agent > Share > Can use.
claims.quote:
Open the agent from the Agents page.
Select the Share ... icon near Publish on the top menu bar.
In the Share panel ... Ensure Can use appears beside the search bar.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; controls[6].note
claims.claim: Makers copy the set-up link and send it to their recipients.
claims.quote:
Select Copy sharing link, then Copy link to set up.
Send the link to the end users you shared the autonomous agent with.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Recipients receive no notification when a maker shares an autonomous agent.
claims.quote: Sharing visibility: Users don't receive a notification when a maker shares an agent with them.

claims.claim: Recipients activate a shared autonomous agent for themselves rather than receiving an automatically running instance.
claims.quote: Recipients can use the can use link to activate the agent for themselves, connect the agent with their own credentials, and manage their permitted trigger settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: An autonomous agent cannot run for a recipient until every trigger, tool and workflow requiring that recipient's credentials is connected.
claims.quote: An autonomous agent can't run until you connect every trigger, tool, and workflow that requires your credentials.

claims.claim: Recipients can edit only trigger options the maker permits through Editable by user.
claims.quote: If you're sharing this agent with others to use, choose which options users can or can't configure themselves by turning on or off Editable by user for each option.

claims.claim: Recipients cannot change instructions, tools or other authoring settings.
claims.quote: You can't change the agent's instructions, tools, or other authoring settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users of a shared autonomous agent cannot specify or modify tool parameters.
claims.quote: Users of a shared autonomous agent can't specify or modify tool parameters.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Tool calls are invoked and executed by AI based on the maker's specifications.
claims.quote: Tool calls are invoked and executed fully with AI, based on the maker's specifications.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: A workflow used as a tool in a shared autonomous agent accepts only end-user credentials.
claims.quote: If your agent calls a workflow as a tool, that workflow can only accept end user credentials for authentication. Workflows that use any maker-only credentials aren't supported for autonomous agents.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Maker updates can require recipients to connect services or consent to changes on the agent management page.
claims.quote: The agent owner can update the agent, which might require you to connect or consent to the updates.

claims.claim: Recipients need to bookmark the management URL for health, repair and update-consent tasks.
claims.quote: End users need to bookmark the agent management URL to check their agent's health, fix the agent, consent to maker updates to the agent, and other management tasks.

claims.claim: Recipients can pause and resume triggers using the Enabled toggle.
claims.quote: To pause a trigger without removing its configuration, turn the Enabled toggle off. Turn it on again when you want the trigger to run.

claims.claim: The agent management Activity tab shows recent runs and failures.
claims.quote: Use the Activity tab to review recent runs and identify failed runs.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk; Scope
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness autonomous agents run from events rather than requiring a person to open a chat.
claims.quote: Use triggers to create autonomous agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness. Autonomous agents run when an event occurs in a connected service.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity
claims.claim: The maker's instructions and tools determine what the agent does with trigger event details.
claims.quote: The trigger sends event details to the agent. Your agent's instructions and tools determine what the agent does with those details.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity
claims.claim: Actions using end-user credentials are constrained by that user's permissions.
claims.quote: The action runs under the end-user's identity. If the user lacks permission for something, the agent is unable to do it on their behalf - by design.

claims.claim: Data policies govern the connectors agents use.
claims.quote: Data policies let you govern how agents connect and interact with data and services, both within and outside your organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited documentation does not explain the treatment of an already-running shared run-only instance after a data-policy change.
claims.quote: Searched: shared autonomous data policy; Copilot Studio shared autonomous agent data policy existing running triggers. Opened admin-data-loss-prevention and the shared-agent setup article; real-time enforcement is stated, but in-flight shared-instance handling is not.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no approval setting specific to run-only shared autonomous agents.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio shared autonomous agent human approval settings; shared autonomous approval. Opened sharing, trigger, setup and autonomous-agents guidance pages; results document design guidance and separate flow approvals, not a run-only sharing approval setting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The agent management article does not state administrator visibility into individual recipients' instances.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous agent run only sharing Dataverse Web API Can use permissions. Opened end-user-manage-shared-agent in full: it documents recipient connections, updates and activity, not administrator instance visibility or maker-departure outcomes.

claims.where: summary; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Usage is metered in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each end user's autonomous usage is totalled and billed through the hosting environment.
claims.quote: Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totaled and billed through the underlying environment where the agent is hosted.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing includes LLM tokens, tools and the harness itself.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Administrators manage and allocate environment credits through the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are managed through the Power Platform admin center. Administrators can allocate credits to environments and monitor usage to ensure that sufficient credits are available.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; controls[6].note; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Sharing prerequisites require recipients to have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user licence.
claims.quote: Users you share with have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user license.

claims.claim: Recipients without a licence can sign up for a trial.
claims.quote: Users who don't have a license can sign up for a trial.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Sharing prerequisites include publishing to Teams + Microsoft 365 with Make agent available in Microsoft Copilot enabled.
claims.quote: Agents you want to share are published to Teams + Microsoft 365, with Make agent available in Microsoft Copilot turned on.

claims.claim: The agent's user authentication prerequisite is Authenticate with Microsoft.
claims.quote: User authentication for the agent is configured to Authenticate with Microsoft.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout; controls[5]
claims.claim: A resource-based spending policy supports a monthly policy limit and optional per-agent limits for selected agents or environments.
claims.quote: Choose No limit or set a monthly spending limit for the policy. You can also set a per-agent limit so that no single agent covered by the policy uses more than the amount you specify.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[5].note; Why it matters
claims.claim: Resource-based spending policies replace covered resources' Power Platform capacity allocations and linked billing plans; existing configuration remains until opting in.
claims.quote: To opt in, create a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy. Until then, your existing Power Platform admin center configuration remains in effect.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[5].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Resource-based spending policies exclude AI Builder credits, so resources using AI Builder should not be moved to them.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies created in the Microsoft 365 admin center don't apply to AI Builder features or the credits they consume. ... Don't move resources, agents, workflows or environments that use AI Builder to these policies.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited pages do not state a credit rate specific to autonomous run-only sharing.
claims.quote: Searched: autonomous run-only credit rates; Microsoft Copilot harness autonomous run credit rates. Opened billing-credit-overview and sharing article; they state the meter and billing environment, not a dedicated run-only rate. Standard-harness rates have a different stated scope.

claims.claim: The cited pages do not describe how shared-autonomous per-recipient usage totals appear in reports.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Copilot harness autonomous run per user usage reports. Opened billing-credit-overview, sharing and Microsoft 365 cost-management pages; they document agent/environment totals, not the presentation of this feature's per-recipient totals.

claims.claim: Editing rights are distinct from run-only sharing and can be assigned through environment security roles.
claims.quote: Add users to the agent's environment, and then assign users editing rights through the environment's security roles.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No dedicated tenant or environment admin switch for Can use autonomous sharing is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous Can use admin sharing switch; Can use sharing admin disable switch approval. Opened sharing, sharing-limits and admin-sharing-controls-limits; found maker sharing and general controls, not a dedicated Can use admin switch.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The feature is user-opt-in: a maker chooses to share and each recipient activates it.
claims.quote: Recipients can use the can use link to activate the agent for themselves, connect the agent with their own credentials, and manage their permitted trigger settings.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining per-user licensing and metered usage.
claims.quote: Users you share with have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user license. ... Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totaled and billed through the underlying environment where the agent is hosted.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating reflects the documented Copilot Credits meter.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Managed Environments sharing controls are at Manage > Environments > environment > Edit Managed Environments > Manage sharing.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environments. ... select a managed environment. ... Edit Managed Environments. ... The sharing rules are located in the Manage sharing section.

claims.claim: The documented Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration call saves the retrieved configuration after its bot sharing extendedSettings are set.
claims.quote: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $governanceConfiguration

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Managed Environments sharing rules are documented for Editor and Viewer permissions, without explicitly identifying Can use autonomous sharing.
claims.quote: Searched: autonomous Can use sharing admin limits; Dataverse Web API Can use permissions. Opened managed-environment-sharing-limits and admin-sharing-controls-limits; both name Editor and Viewer, not autonomous Can use permissions.

claims.claim: The data-policy creation path runs through Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Add an environment > environment > Add to policy > Assign connectors.
claims.quote: To add an environment to your data policy, select the environment in the Available tab, and then select Add to policy.
claims.fix: Insert the selection tab: Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Add an environment > Available > environment > Add to policy > Assign connectors.

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy creates a policy but its reference does not describe classifying the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector.
claims.quote:
New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy
Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.
-DefaultConnectorClassification
Default connector classification.
claims.fix: Replace 'its page describes no connector classification' in the row note and prose with 'its reference does not describe assigning the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector to Blocked'. The reference does document DefaultConnectorClassification.

claims.claim: The data-policy article requires tenant-admin or Environment Admin permissions.
claims.quote: Be a tenant admin or have the Environment Admin role.

claims.where: controls[2]; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector prevents adding event triggers and produces a Triggers-section error.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from adding event triggers ... configure a data policy that blocks the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector. ... a detailed error message appears in the Triggers section on the Overview page.

claims.claim: Ungrouped environments expose Control maker credential options under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... Select Environments or Environment groups. ... select Settings ... Expand the Product section, and select Features. ... Copilot Studio agents ... Under Control maker credential options

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for Control maker credential options is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Control maker credential options API PowerShell; maker credentials Set-TenantSettings; Update-EnvironmentSettings; Power Platform API pac admin settings Dataverse organization. Opened configure-no-maker-authentication and Environment Management Settings Update; no setting payload found.

claims.claim: Blocking maker credentials changes authentication requirements for all agents in the affected environment.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The maker-credential article warns that blocking maker credentials causes scheduled or autonomous background agents to fail for missing credentials.
claims.quote: As a result, agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials.

claims.claim: Grouped environments must use Manage > Environment groups > group > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options.
claims.quote: You can't configure this feature on the individual details page for environments that are in a group, you must use the group's details page.

claims.claim: Configuring maker credential options for a grouped environment requires a tenant administrator with access to the group.
claims.quote: If the environment you want to configure is part of an environment group, you must be a tenant admin with access to the group.

claims.claim: The embedded-maker-credentials control is at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features > Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.
claims.quote: Go to Manage > Environments ... select the environment ... Select Settings, and then select Features. ... Find Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.
claims.fix: Retain the cited path, but add this qualification to the row note: 'The Power Platform preview article documents another route: Security > Threat detection > Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials > Environments > environment > Set up.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/security/control-sharing-agents-with-embedded-maker-credentials.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for the embedded-maker-credentials sharing control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials API PowerShell Dataverse; maker credentials Power Platform API pac admin settings; Dataverse reference maker credentials. Opened the control article and environment settings API; no documented control payload found.

claims.claim: The embedded-maker-credentials control governs sharing and publishing, not a running agent.
claims.quote: The sharing agents with embedded maker credentials control governs sharing and publishing. It doesn't block an agent while the agent is running.

claims.claim: The embedded-maker-credentials control does not retroactively unshare or disable existing agents.
claims.quote: Enabling enforcement doesn't retroactively unshare or disable agents that were previously shared.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed how the embedded-maker-credentials sharing control applies to Can use sharing.
claims.quote: Connections configured to use end-user credentials aren't subject to this connection-sharing restriction because each user authenticates by using their own connection at runtime.
claims.fix: Replace the embedded-control uncertainty in the row note and Governance controls with: 'Connections configured to use end-user credentials are not subject to this connection-sharing restriction; run-only sharing requires triggers and tools configured for user authentication.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-sharing-controls-limits and the existing sharing article. Remove the embedded-maker-credentials clause from the corresponding Open questions item, leaving the Managed Environments sharing-limits question unchanged.

claims.claim: Resource-based spending policies are created at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management.
Select Configuration, and then select Add spending policy.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for agent/environment resource-based spending policies is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph resource based spending policies Copilot Studio API create limit. Opened Copilot Cost Management API overview and resource-policy UI article; the API documents all-user/group audience policies, not agent/environment resource scoping.

claims.claim: The cost-management article recommends the AI Administrator role for Power Platform or Dynamics 365 administrators managing spending policies.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator or Dynamics 365 Administrator | AI Administrator | Manage spending policies.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 resource-based spending controls take precedence over Power Platform spending controls for covered resources.
claims.quote: If a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center covers the environment or agent, its controls take precedence over the Power Platform admin center controls for that usage.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for granting Can use access to shared autonomous agents is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous agent run only sharing Dataverse Web API Can use permissions; Can use autonomous API sharing. Opened authoring-share-agent; searched Power Platform CLI and Dataverse sharing references; no autonomous Can use grant operation found.

claims.claim: Credit consumption can be reviewed by agent and environment.
claims.quote: You can view consumption by environment and agent.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to check consumption by environment and agent, but the controls table has no reporting row.
claims.quote: Check Copilot Credit consumption by environment and agent against the maker's estimate. The table covers sharing, triggers, credentials, spending limits and recipient access, but not consumption reporting.
claims.fix: Remove 'Check Copilot Credit consumption by environment and agent against the maker's estimate' from the After rollout checklist; that reporting control has no corresponding table row.
